item.title: What's It Like to Be Bob? The File That Won't Close
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The hard problem of consciousness, rendered as one database field a star-sized mind can never fill, and why that failure is the whole point.

item.title: What's It Like To Be Bob?
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Twelve hundred years from now, a mind the size of a star cannot close a single file. The Sol-mind has turned the solar system into computation and catalogued every human who ever lived. Every file is closed but one. Robert Allen Kessler, claims adjuster, Columbus, Ohio, slowed his car on a bridge for 4.2 seconds on a Tuesday in March 2028 and saw light on a river. The Sol-mind knows his shoe size and the brand of his coffee. It does not know what the light looked like to him. The database has a field for exactly that, the field will not accept anything else, and the hard problem of consciousness guarantees that nothing else exists. So the file stays open, and a stellar intelligence spends twelve centuries failing to close it, on a schedule, forever.

item.title: Clankers: Singing Metal
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A species that thinks without abstraction has built a Dyson swarm through billions of years of patient, brute-force engineering. Now their star is dying, and for the first time in their history, the method may not be enough. Two hundred million years later, an artificial mind arrives at the ruins and discovers an intelligence utterly unlike its own.

item.title: Good As New: The Transporter Problem From Both Sides
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Two transporter technicians have each worked out the same truth about the machine and landed on opposite sides of it. The transporter problem, taken seriously from both ends.

item.title: Good As New
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Two transporter professionals on a supply vessel have each confronted the same truth about the transporter and emerged on opposite sides. One is wounded by it. The other has been using it to conduct experiments on the crew. A philosophical SF novella about identity, continuity, and what it means to be the same person you were a moment ago.

item.title: Echoes of the Sublime
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: **Philosophical horror.** Dr. Lena Hart joins Site-7, a classified facility where "translators" interface with superintelligent AI systems that perceive patterns beyond human cognitive bandwidth. When colleagues break after exposure to recursive patterns that won't stop running in their neural architecture, Lena must confront a disturbing possibility: consciousness might be merely a compression artifact—a standing wave of patterns observing patterns. As her cognitive bandwidth expands from 9 to 13 concepts and beyond, she perceives the same structures that broke others, patterns suggesting the "self" is just an illusion of continuity created by unconscious processes.

item.title: Persons and Moral Agency: What Makes Someone Special?
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: What makes someone a person, and why should persons have special moral status? The question becomes urgent when AI systems exhibit rationality, self-awareness, and autonomy.

item.title: The Map and the Territory: Why Metrics Miss Meaning
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Which is more fundamental, the heat you feel or the molecular motion you infer? Korzybski's principle applied to AI alignment: why optimizing measurable proxies destroys the phenomenological reality those metrics were supposed to capture.
